a4-b141-signs: If a trip comes with diarrhea or nausea, a toxic heaviness or a dirty body-feeling, or jaw tension, the mind may feel like it's going crazy because the gut or the brain is going crazy. The same goes for loss of bodily control (someone wetting or soiling themselves, or not being able to sit up, stand, walk or talk) and for neurological disorganization, my catch-all for that loss of control plus a whole lot more. Losing control of the body like that is on the list to call medics for, and the brain checks further up show what else to look for.
a5-b141-do: Those trips are what the remedies below are for, and the shadow work further down is for a mainly emotional crisis. If you're in mental hell and gut hell at the same time, address the gut first with the gut tools. You don't need to try to tell which is from what. A gut-driven mental hell is often mistaken as shadow work.
a4-gutintro:
The gut tools are the first things I would use, even preventively on the come-up (while the drug is still kicking in), because I want to address possible toxins before I put the distress down to something more mysterious, like a spiritual sign.

After all, nausea and diarrhea are common on psychedelics, and people generally don't feel good mentally during the nausea and gut pain parts of the come-up. Diarrhea can be a flushing out of toxins, and usually there's a lot of relief once everything starts coming out in the toilet. But severe diarrhea can flush out too much fluid, and being badly dried out is on the list to call medics for. Still, you shouldn't have a lot of gut discomfort if the toxins in the gut get bound, which is what the tools below do, and dosing lower on the psychedelic helps too.
